provisionalCases.sourceLocator: Build Back Better Fact Sheet / Build worker power, raise wages, and secure stronger benefits
provisionalCases.pledgeParaphrase: Raise the nationwide federal minimum wage to $15 per hour.
provisionalCases.successCriterion: Federal minimum wage of $15 per hour applicable to covered workers nationally, rather than only to federal contractors.

events.description: The Senate-printed H.R. 1319 proposal contained Subtitle B, section 2101, to phase in a $15 federal minimum wage; it did not become enacted law in that form.
Executive Order 14026 required a $15 minimum for covered federal contract workers; did not establish a nationwide private-sector wage floor.
External assessment finds the nationwide federal minimum remained at $7.25 and the national pledge was not enacted.
Successor administration revoked the contractor-specific executive order; do not score this as Biden's end-term pledge outcome.

ambiguityNotes: The legislative route included a procedural constraint; evidence does not demonstrate every possible legislative path was impossible.
Narrower contractor coverage is implementation activity, not attainment of a nationwide statutory minimum wage.
Policy reversal in 2025 is recorded as persistence information, not scored against Biden's 2021–2025 term.
Separate campaign commitments to end tipped subminimum wages and subminimum wages for workers with disabilities are intentionally not evaluated within this atomic nationwide $15 pledge.
A previous unverified PolitiFact deep-link identifier has been replaced with the article URL independently retrieved in the public source audit.

provisionalCases.sourceLocator: Combating the Climate Crisis and Pursuing Environmental Justice / public land protections
provisionalCases.pledgeParaphrase: Restore federal monument protections for the Bears Ears landscape.
provisionalCases.successCriterion: Federal restoration of Bears Ears National Monument protections through proclamation.

events.description: Proclamation 10285 expanded the Bears Ears National Monument reservation to approximately 1.36 million acres.
A successor proclamation reduced the monument reservation to approximately 121,096 acres; this does not change the 2021–2025 fulfillment assessment.

ambiguityNotes: This atom tests Bears Ears restoration only, not the platform's other national monuments and public lands.
Later modification is recorded as durability, not attributed to Biden's in-term behavior.
A proclamation can be contested; this entry does not adjudicate litigation or legal finality.

provisionalCases.sourceLocator: Creating a 21st Century Immigration System / rescind national emergency
provisionalCases.pledgeParaphrase: Terminate the national emergency declaration used to redirect funds for a southern border wall.
provisionalCases.successCriterion: The national emergency invoked for the border wall is formally terminated.

events.description: Proclamation 10142 formally terminated the border-wall national emergency and directed a review of diverted funds.
The successor's proclamation revoked Proclamation 10142 on the first day of the following administration.

ambiguityNotes: Terminating the emergency is the test, not whether all border-wall spending ended.
The January 20, 2025 reversal belongs to the successor administration and is recorded as durability only.
The campaign platform also made other border-wall commitments; these require separate records.

provisionalCases.sourceLocator: Rebuilding America's Tool of First Resort / rejoin and reform the UN Human Rights Council
provisionalCases.pledgeParaphrase: Restore U.S. membership in the United Nations Human Rights Council.
provisionalCases.successCriterion: The United States is elected and begins serving a regular term as UN Human Rights Council member.

events.description: United States elected to UN Human Rights Council for the 2022–2024 term.
Membership term began; UN official membership lists include the U.S. for 2022.

ambiguityNotes: This record tests Council membership only, not the separate pledge to reform the Council.
Election to the Council required votes from other member states; this is not unilateral action.

provisionalCases.sourceLocator: Mobilizing the World to Address Transnational Challenges / Climate Change / Kigali Amendment
provisionalCases.pledgeParaphrase: Secure U.S. ratification of the Kigali Amendment to the Montreal Protocol.
provisionalCases.successCriterion: The U.S. deposits an instrument of ratification and the treaty becomes effective for the U.S.

events.description: U.S. Senate gave advice and consent to ratification, confirmed by State Department.
The United Nations Treaty Collection records U.S. ratification on October 31, 2022.
The Amendment entered into force for the United States, per the UN Treaty Collection.

ambiguityNotes: The Kigali clause also promised domestic hydrofluorocarbon phaseout; this atom measures treaty ratification only.
Senate advice and consent, instrument deposit, and legal entry into force are separate milestones.

provisionalCases.sourceLocator: Combating the Climate Crisis and Pursuing Environmental Justice / Paris Agreement; also Climate Change
provisionalCases.pledgeParaphrase: Rejoin the Paris Climate Agreement promptly after taking office.
provisionalCases.successCriterion: United States becomes a party to the Paris Agreement again.

events.description: President signed the instrument of acceptance.
The United States officially became a party again.

ambiguityNotes: Party platform language contains multiple climate commitments; only Paris reentry is coded here.
Outcome at February 2021 does not infer later administrations' policy or persistence.
A previously stored PolitiFact deep link could not be verified; it has been removed pending source-link review.

provisionalCases.sourceLocator: Creating a 21st Century Immigration System / immediately terminate travel and immigration bans
provisionalCases.pledgeParaphrase: End the previous administration's targeted travel and entry bans affecting primarily Muslim and African countries.
provisionalCases.successCriterion: The specified Trump-era entry bans are formally revoked by federal presidential action.

events.description: Proclamation 10141 revoked specified earlier orders and proclamations restricting entry.

ambiguityNotes: The promise to invite denied visa applicants to reapply is a separate atomic commitment not scored here.
Repeal of the named orders is not evidence that no replacement restriction existed or was later enacted.
The proclamation concerns specific orders; this entry does not rate all immigration restrictions.

provisionalCases.sourceLocator: Rebuilding America's Tool of First Resort / Rejoin and reform the WHO
provisionalCases.pledgeParaphrase: Restore participation in the World Health Organization by withdrawing the previous administration's announced plan to exit.
provisionalCases.successCriterion: The U.S. reverses its 2020 notice of intent to withdraw from WHO and remains a member.

events.description: President Biden informed the UN Secretary-General that the U.S. retracts the July 2020 notice of intent to withdraw from WHO.

ambiguityNotes: The U.S. had not legally completed withdrawal, so this is a rescission of a pending withdrawal, not literal re-accession.
The original platform also pledged WHO reform; this record tests only restored participation.
The American Presidency Project notes an original copy of the letter was not available for its verification.
